title: PowerPoint: Copilot for creating and editing presentations in GCC
summary: Hold: the briefing understates possible licence costs and treats the data-access boundary as undocumented even though Microsoft documents Copilot's permission-based access. The roadmap facts and licence-assignment instructions are supported, and the briefing correctly reports the conflicting GCC availability information.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions
claims.claim: How access to users' source files, meetings and emails is scoped for this feature is not documented.

claims.where: front matter: cost; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Cost is low, meaning indirect cost only, although the page also budgets an add-on licence for users who do not hold it.
claims.quote: Treat the cost as the add-on licence for users who do not hold it, plus admin and training time. / Low. ... the add-on licence itself is bought separately, so the cost is admin and adoption time.
claims.fix: Set cost to 'medium' and replace the cost rationale with 'Medium. Users who do not already hold Microsoft 365 Copilot need the add-on licence; existing licensed users have admin and adoption costs. The cited pages document no separate PowerPoint-specific charge or meter.' This matches the scale for add-on licences for a subset of users rather than indirect cost only.
